context: Each move climbs 1 or 2 stairs. Let dp[i] be the number of ways to reach stair i. The diagram fills the dynamic programming table from the bottom up without a recursive call stack.
description: Set dp[1] = 1 and dp[2] = 2. From dp[3] through dp[9], calculate dp[i] = dp[i − 1] + dp[i − 2] in order. Each term depends only on its two predecessors, both of which are already available.

Nine boxes in a row show only the state names dp[1] through dp[9]. The initial values dp[1] = 1 and dp[2] = 2 and the recurrence appear below. The values 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, and the result 55 for dp[9] follow from the base cases and formula. They are not labels inside the boxes. The table lists the base cases, dependencies, and derived results.

frames.explanation: Bottom-up iteration computes each state once and stops at the target. Applying the recurrence to the initial values shown gives 55 ways for the target dp[9].
frames.title: Counting ways to climb stairs iteratively from the base cases

summary: Start with dp[1] = 1 and dp[2] = 2. Add the preceding two terms at each step, working from left to right through dp[9].
